t: The Secretary of the Air Force may establish or develop Air Force installations and facilities by proceeding with construction made necessary by changes in Air Force missions and responsibilities which have been occasioned by : (a) unforeseen security considerations, (b) new weapons developments, (c) new and unforeseen research and development requirements, or (d) improved production schedules, if the. Secretary of Defense determines that deferral of such construction for inclusion in the next Military Construction Authorization Act would be inconsistent with interests of national security, and in connection therewith to acquire, construct, convert, rehabilitate, or install permanent or temporary public works, including hind acquisition, site preparation, appurtenances, utilities, and equipment in the total amount of $10,000,000: Provided, That the Secretary of the Air Force, or his designee, shall notify the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives, immediately upon reaching a final decision to implement, of the cost, of construction of any public work undertaken under this section, including those real estate actions pertaining thereto. This authorization will expire as of September 30, 1969, except for those public work projects concerning which the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives have been notified pursuant to this section prior to that date.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the notification requirement and the Secretary of Defense's determination amount to consultative procedure. Both stay inside the federal government: the notice goes to congressional committees, and the determination is made by a federal official. No state, local, private, expert, or public party is consulted, and the section provides for no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue.
fable.s: shall notify the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives, immediately upon reaching a final decision to implement

opus.w: The only procedure in this section is a notice to congressional committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. The other decision step is the Secretary of Defense's national-security determination, which is also inside the government. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, or given a right to object, so this is not participation.
opus.s: the Secretary of the Air Force, or his designee, shall notify the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives, immediately upon reaching a final decision to implement, of the cost, of construction of any public work undertaken under this section
opus.b: 1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The proviso sets up a formal step: the Secretary must notify the Armed Services Committees of the Senate and the House before projects go ahead. That looks like a review procedure. But the only actors are the Secretary of the Air Force, the Secretary of Defense and committees of Congress, and all of them are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is involved, and the section creates no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of the Air Force to notify the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Notification to internal government bodies does not constitute participation with outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: Provided, That the Secretary of the Air Force, or his designee, shall notify the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives, immediately upon reaching a final decision to implement, of the cost, of construction of any public work undertaken under this section
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that notifying the Committees on Armed Services constitutes "participation" because it involves external oversight or consultation before a decision is finalized. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress, its committees, and its members are INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, reporting to or notifying Congress is intra-governmental communication, not participation with outside parties.
